subject: Clarify billing language: billable units, streaming tokens, and rounding
messages:
From: Claire Reynolds <claire@neonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neon Health Procurement <procurement@neonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on billing units / streaming tokens for Hosted API

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the call earlier. We’re close on economics but the legal team pushed back on two items they want explicitly called out in the SOW and exhibit:

1) Definition of "billable tokens" — specifically whether we bill on raw model tokens, normalized tokens, or a packaged definition for streaming responses.
2) Rounding rules — they’d like to avoid per-stream rounding that could materially increase monthly spend for high-volume short responses.

Two quick examples they gave (attached are sample transcripts):
- A 3-token model prompt with a 2-token streamed response — how is that rounded?
- Long streaming sessions where the client receives partial events frequently.

Can you provide the exact clause language you expect to include in the contract and any examples we can forward to legal? We’d prefer firm language rather than hand-wavy bullets.

Appreciate it — Claire
Claire Reynolds
VP, Product
Neon Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire@neonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on billing units / streaming tokens for Hosted API

Claire — thanks for laying out the asks. I looped in Ben (pricing) and Laura (billing/legal intake).

High level: Redwood bills on "billable tokens" which we define as the number of model tokens generated and consumed after our normalization layer (removes transport framing and maps different model vocabularies to a standard unit). For streaming we provide two options in contracts:

Option A (default): Continuous per-token accounting — every token emitted by the model is billable. Rounding occurs per-request to the nearest whole token (no per-event rounding beyond token granularity). For SSE/websocket streams the server-side token counter is authoritative.

Option B (streaming-friendly): Aggregate-minute rounding — we sum tokens per client connection per minute and round the minute total (helps with high-frequency partial events). This option is typically paired with a small usage premium or a minimum commit to protect economics.

I’ll paste a short, copy-ready clause below (Ben — feel free to refine). If Neon prefers Option B we can provide exact pricing delta.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, MidMarket & Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Claire / Hannah — draft clause and examples attached. I tried to be precise so legal can paste into the SOW. Key points:

- "Billable Token" definition: A billable token equals one token unit after Redwood’s normalization mapping. Normalization removes network framing and non-semantic control bytes; tokens are counted post-tokenizer.

- Streaming: For requests where the Model returns incremental chunks (streaming), tokens will be counted when emitted by the server. If a request is interrupted, only emitted tokens are billable; buffered/non-emitted tokens are not billed.

- Rounding: Billable tokens are summed at the request level and rounded down to the nearest whole token (i.e., fractional token counts are aggregated and rounded to whole tokens). To address Neon’s short-response concern we offer the aggregate-minute rounding (Option B) as an alternative: tokens emitted over any 60-second window for a single client connection will be summed and rounded to the nearest whole token.

- Commit tiers: We recommend linking the client’s committed monthly token bucket to the normalized billable tokens and allowing a 5% overage buffer billed at the committed rate; amounts above 105% are billed at the overage rate. True-ups occur monthly.

I attached: redwood-billable-units-appendix.docx (contract text), usage-example-streaming.md (two worked examples), and the commit schedule spreadsheet. Let me know if you want me to redline the contract directly.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales Engineering

From: Neon Health Procurement <procurement@neonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on billing units / streaming tokens for Hosted API

Hannah / Ben — thanks for the detail and the examples. A couple of legal procurement asks before we move to signature:

1) The clause that says "rounded down to the nearest whole token" looks favorable to Redwood in the short-response case. We prefer a neutral approach that neither party is advantaged by definition. Can you consider "round to the nearest whole token" with ties rounded down?

2) For streaming, we need an explicit definition of what counts as a single "client connection" (SSE vs WebSocket vs long-polling). Our use case uses frequent short SSE fragments (10–30 bytes) on many concurrent connections; aggregate-minute rounding would materially lower our invoice compared to per-request rounding.

3) Please confirm there will be a billable token accounting report delivered monthly with per-minute and per-connection breakdowns (CSV export) for audit.

We’re close — if Redwood can accept the tie-breaker rounding and add the connection definition and monthly report commitment, we can proceed to signature and the committed tier.

Procurement Team
Neon Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire@neonhealth.com>, Neon Health Procurement <procurement@neonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on billing units / streaming tokens for Hosted API

Claire / Procurement — good points. Agreed items and next steps below: 

- Rounding: Redwood will adopt "round to the nearest whole token; in the event of a 0.5 tie, round down." We'll update the appendix with that exact text.

- Connection definition: "Client connection" is defined as a unique transport session between the client and Redwood’s ingress (identified by connection ID and transport type). Transport types supported for this SOW: WebSocket and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Long-polling is treated as discrete requests (request-level rounding applies). We’ll add an example in the appendix showing an SSE session with minute aggregation.

- Reporting: Redwood will provide a monthly CSV export containing per-minute token aggregates by connection ID and per-request token counts for the billing period for audit and reconciliation. We’ll include a sample CSV in the onboarding packet.

Ben / Laura: please prepare an updated appendix with the tie-breaker rounding language, the connection definition clause, and a one-paragraph description of the monthly report format. I’ll coordinate execution once the doc is updated. Neon — we’ll also include the Option B aggregate-minute rounding in the SOW as the elected behavior for your account.

Proposed timeline: updated appendix by EOD Wed 8/26, internal review Thurs, signature-ready DocuSign sent Fri.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, MidMarket & Healthcare
Redwood Inference
